# Question

Do FTCS and Crank--Nicolson reproduce the declared single-mode heat equation,
converge at their expected rates, and preserve the distinction between linear
stability and monotonicity?

# Conditions and method

The dimensionless problem is

$$
\frac{\partial\theta}{\partial Fo}=\frac{\partial^2\theta}{\partial\xi^2},
\qquad
\theta(0,Fo)=\theta(1,Fo)=0,
\qquad
\theta(\xi,0)=\sin(\pi\xi),
$$

with continuous reference
$\theta_{\mathrm{ref}}=\exp(-\pi^2Fo)\sin(\pi\xi)$. Combined refinement ends
at $Fo=0.1$, uses interval counts 10 through 160, and fixes
$r=\Delta Fo/(\Delta\xi)^2=0.4$. Isolated temporal refinement fixes 20
intervals and uses 80 through 1280 steps.

# Results

![Numerical fields at 40 intervals, compared with the continuous
reference.](figures/solution_overlay/output/solution_overlay.png){width=78%}

![Combined and isolated-temporal refinement results retained by the analysis
set.](figures/refinement/output/refinement.png){width=82%}

| Study | Method | Finest error | Finest observed order |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Combined | FTCS | $1.654619\times10^{-5}$ | 2.000230 |
| Combined | Crank--Nicolson | $1.181738\times10^{-5}$ | 1.999746 |
| Temporal | FTCS | $1.415673\times10^{-4}$ | 1.000467 |
| Temporal | Crank--Nicolson | $1.814958\times10^{-8}$ | 2.000004 |

Every finest error is below its retained Richardson-based value bound. The
combined path recovers second-order behavior for both methods. Removing spatial
error recovers first-order FTCS and second-order Crank--Nicolson temporal
behavior.

![Worst-grid-mode amplification distinguishes bounded amplification from
monotonic decay.](figures/amplification/output/amplification.png){width=68%}

FTCS crosses $G=-1$ at $r=0.5$. Crank--Nicolson remains linearly stable for
positive $r$ but can change sign, so it is not unconditionally monotone.

# Interpretation and limitations

The retained values support code and solution verification for one smooth
Fourier mode on a uniform one-dimensional grid with constant coefficients and
exact homogeneous boundaries. They do not validate a physical heat-transfer
model or cover nonsmooth fields, variable coefficients, nonlinear sources, or
multidimensional operators.

The exact values displayed here come from CSV files below `figures/*/output/`.
Generation, rendering, and independent checks remain in `scripts/` and do not
run from this notebook.
